raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

This PR adds native MUSA compilation to SGLang's Ninja-based JIT build path.
The MUSA branch selects `mcc`, passes `-x musa` and
`--offload-arch=mp_*`, and uses MUSA include paths and runtime libraries.
HIP retains precedence, and CUDA remains the fallback.

MUSA JIT uses C++20, aligned with the LLVM20-based mtcc20x path. CUDA and HIP
retain C++20. Shared JIT headers use the upstream C++20 facilities directly;
SGLang no longer carries a duplicate C++17 compatibility layer. The JIT cache
fingerprints the selected compiler path and version.

Runtime and FP8 aliases are supplied by TorchADA through
`stable_compat_include_dir()`. This path depends on
[yingzhou-bjtu/torchada#4](https://github.com/MooreThreads/torchada/pull/132),
currently a fork Draft. A TorchADA release containing that change is required
before this PR can be merged.

[sgl-project/sglang-omni#2442](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/2442)
is the downstream consumer integration: it exposes the existing joint-RoPE
provider on MUSA. JIT compilation remains in SGLang.

Part of #16565.

## Validation

Recorded real mtcc20x evidence: MTT S5000, LLVM20-based `mcc` (clang 20.1.8),
`--offload-arch=mp_31`; 5.3 GA `mcc3` and M1000 were not verified.

- Static checks pass in the current worktree; the recorded mtcc20x focused cache run passed `67 tests` before this C++20-only cleanup.
- The current source selects `mcc`, `-x musa`, `--offload-arch=mp_31`,
  `-DUSE_MUSA`, and `-std=c++20` for MUSA JIT; the recorded mtcc20x run
  confirmed matching host/device standard flags.
- Recorded mtcc20x evidence: `fused_rope` real MUSA JIT build, module load,
  and numerical smoke passed; `q_max_abs_error=0.0`, `k_max_abs_error=0.0`.
- Recorded mtcc20x evidence: `speculative_tree` and `ngram_embedding` real
  MUSA JIT build and module load passed.
- `speculative_sampling`: dependency-blocked because
  `flashinfer/sampling.cuh` is absent from the validation image.

### C++ standard decision

The recorded LLVM20-based mtcc20x probe passed the public-header closure in
C++20 (`bits.h`, `utils.h`, `tensor.h`, `type.cuh`, and `utils.cuh`). The MUSA
JIT path therefore uses C++20 directly, matching the CUDA/HIP upstream model.
The legacy clang14 path and M1000 remain explicit follow-up evidence items;
this PR does not claim they were freshly verified.

## MUSA JIT Build Overview

The production inventory below is generated from every `load_jit` call site
under `python/sglang/kernels/ops/**/*.py`: 194 call sites and 165 unique source
selections. Build, load, runtime smoke, dependency, and backend-specific
states are kept separate.

| Operator / module | Source | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fused_rope` | `csrc/elementwise/rope.cuh` | `PASS_BUILD_LOAD_SMOKE`; numerical smoke passed |
| `speculative_tree` | `csrc/speculative/tree.cuh` | `PASS_BUILD_LOAD` |
| `ngram_embedding` | `csrc/speculative/ngram_embedding.cuh` | `PASS_BUILD_LOAD` |
| `speculative_sampling` | `csrc/speculative/sampling.cuh` | `BLOCKED_DEPENDENCY`; `flashinfer/sampling.cuh` is unavailable in the validation image |

| --- | --- |
| `PASS_BUILD_LOAD_SMOKE` | Real MUSA `mcc` build, module load, and numerical smoke |
| `PASS_BUILD_LOAD` | Real MUSA `mcc` build and module load |

## Overview

This PR adds native MUSA compilation to SGLang's Ninja-based JIT build path.
The MUSA branch selects `mcc`, passes `-x musa` and
`--offload-arch=mp_*`, and uses MUSA include paths and runtime libraries.
HIP retains precedence, and CUDA remains the fallback.

MUSA JIT uses C++20, aligned with the LLVM20-based mtcc20x path. CUDA and HIP
retain C++20. Shared JIT headers use the upstream C++20 facilities directly;
SGLang no longer carries a duplicate C++17 compatibility layer. The JIT cache
fingerprints the selected compiler path and version.

Runtime and FP8 aliases are supplied by TorchADA through
`stable_compat_include_dir()`. This path depends on
[yingzhou-bjtu/torchada#4](https://github.com/MooreThreads/torchada/pull/132),
currently a fork Draft. A TorchADA release containing that change is required
before this PR can be merged.

[sgl-project/sglang-omni#2442](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/2442)
is the downstream consumer integration: it exposes the existing joint-RoPE
provider on MUSA. JIT compilation remains in SGLang.

Part of #16565.

## Validation

Recorded real mtcc20x evidence: MTT S5000, LLVM20-based `mcc` (clang 20.1.8),
`--offload-arch=mp_31`; 5.3 GA `mcc3` and M1000 were not verified.

- Static checks pass in the current worktree; the recorded mtcc20x focused cache run passed `67 tests` before this C++20-only cleanup.
- The current source selects `mcc`, `-x musa`, `--offload-arch=mp_31`,
  `-DUSE_MUSA`, and `-std=c++20` for MUSA JIT; the recorded mtcc20x run
  confirmed matching host/device standard flags.
- Recorded mtcc20x evidence: `fused_rope` real MUSA JIT build, module load,
  and numerical smoke passed; `q_max_abs_error=0.0`, `k_max_abs_error=0.0`.
- Recorded mtcc20x evidence: `speculative_tree` and `ngram_embedding` real
  MUSA JIT build and module load passed.
- `speculative_sampling`: dependency-blocked because
  `flashinfer/sampling.cuh` is absent from the validation image.

### C++ standard decision

The recorded LLVM20-based mtcc20x probe passed the public-header closure in
C++20 (`bits.h`, `utils.h`, `tensor.h`, `type.cuh`, and `utils.cuh`). The MUSA
JIT path therefore uses C++20 directly, matching the CUDA/HIP upstream model.
The legacy clang14 path and M1000 remain explicit follow-up evidence items;
this PR does not claim they were freshly verified.
